history.body: Hi, I saw the listing. We’re looking for a bit more room for the family. Is the living area comfortable for everyday family use?

The living, dining and kitchen are arranged open-plan, so your family can share one connected everyday space. The 900 sq. ft. layout also avoids a long internal corridor, helping make more of the space usable, and there’s an entrance foyer before the living area for a little privacy. A viewing would let you judge how the layout feels for your family.
That sounds promising, but I’m trying to picture it with the kids and a dining table. Do you have a floor plan you can share?

I’ll check for the approved floor plan and share it if available. That should help you picture how a dining table could fit in the living area with the kids; I don’t want to guess at furniture fit without seeing the plan.

Thanks for checking instead of guessing. The open layout sounds useful with the kids, but my partner would prefer to see the layout first before we arrange a viewing. I’ll check with them and get back to you.

Of course—it makes sense to look at the plan together first. I don’t want to guess about dining-table fit; once the approved Type A plan is confirmed as shareable, I’ll send it over so you and your partner can see whether the open living and dining space works for family meals before deciding about a visit.
